column1: # The libraries the executables link, in the order their command file names them, then the kit's other
# files. A member list names the library's modules written in source, in that list's order (the order
# the linker breaks a tie between two definitions by). The kit file is the library as Sony shipped it,
# by its SHA-256: a library built from its members departs from it only where the original's did, and
# lists its commons as the kit's does (plain, as Sony's 3.6 archives and PSYLIB 1.04; marked by a
# leading zero byte, as PSYLIB 2.x and Sony's 3.7 LIBGPU). Two links take each library, and both give
# the executables' SHA-256 in builds.tsv: "source link" says how a link from this tree's library
# source takes it, the link by which that source was checked, and "build.sh takes" what this tree's
# build.sh puts in its own link. Where every module the executables take from a library is written in
# source, the kit file adds nothing and a link may leave it unread. A row naming a release is another
# release's archive of its library, which neither link reads: each module the executables link is the
# member of the kit's file or of such an archive that its bytes equal.
